Product guides: Integrated Logic Analyzer (PG172) and System ILA (PG261); VLNV version suffixes vary by release.

tools.name: VIO / JTAG to AXI Master / Debug Bridge (vio, jtag_axi, debug_bridge)
tools.description: Debug cores that drive the design rather than only observe it. VIO provides virtual inputs and outputs that are read and written from the Hardware Manager, which is the easiest way to toggle a control bit or read a status word without a processor. JTAG to AXI Master issues real AXI read and write transactions from Tcl, so peripheral registers and memories can be exercised with no software at all. Debug Bridge routes the debug network to somewhere other than the device's own JTAG pins, for example over PCIe or from the PS.
tools.usage:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:vio:3.0 vio_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:jtag_axi:1.2 jtag_axi_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:debug_bridge:3.0 debug_bridge_0

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_NUM_PROBE_IN / CONFIG.C_NUM_PROBE_OUT (vio)
parameters.description: Number of monitored inputs and driven outputs.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_PROBE_IN<n>_WIDTH / C_PROBE_OUT<n>_WIDTH (vio)
parameters.description: Width in bits of each probe.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_PROBE_OUT<n>_INIT_VAL (vio)
parameters.description: Value an output probe drives after configuration and before the Hardware Manager changes it.

parameters.name: CONFIG.PROTOCOL (jtag_axi)
parameters.description: AXI protocol presented by the master, AXI4 or AXI4-Lite.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_DEBUG_MODE (debug_bridge)
parameters.description: Selects which debug path the bridge implements, for example from BSCAN to the debug hub or from an AXI master into the debug network.

parameters.name: create_hw_axi_txn / run_hw_axi
parameters.description: Hardware Manager commands used to issue transactions through a jtag_axi core.

tools.example:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:vio:3.0 vio_0
set_property -dict [list CONFIG.C_NUM_PROBE_IN {1} CONFIG.C_PROBE_IN0_WIDTH {32} \
  CONFIG.C_NUM_PROBE_OUT {1} CONFIG.C_PROBE_OUT0_WIDTH {4}] [get_bd_cells vio_0]

create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:jtag_axi:1.2 jtag_axi_0
connect_bd_intf_net [get_bd_intf_pins jtag_axi_0/M_AXI] [get_bd_intf_pins smartconnect_0/S02_AXI]
assign_bd_address

# Later, in the Hardware Manager: read a peripheral register over JTAG
open_hw_manager
create_hw_axi_txn rd_gpio [get_hw_axis hw_axi_1] -address 41200000 -len 1 -type read
run_hw_axi rd_gpio
puts [get_property DATA [get_hw_axi_txns rd_gpio]]
tools.notes: A jtag_axi master must be given an address mapping with assign_bd_address like any other master, or its transactions decode to nothing. VIO outputs are asynchronous to the design clock, so drive only static control bits with them, never anything that needs a clean single-cycle pulse. Product guides: VIO (PG159), JTAG to AXI Master (PG174), Debug Bridge (PG245); VLNV version suffixes vary by release.

tools.name: Utility cores (xlconstant, xlconcat, xlslice, util_vector_logic)
tools.description: The small glue blocks that make a block design expressible without dropping to RTL: xlconstant ties a signal to a fixed value, xlconcat bundles several scalars or vectors into one wider vector, xlslice extracts a bit range out of a vector, and util_vector_logic performs a single AND, OR, XOR or NOT across a vector. They cost almost no resources and appear in nearly every non-trivial design, most often to invert a reset or to gather interrupt lines into a processor's interrupt port.
tools.usage:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xlconstant:1.1 xlconstant_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xlconcat:2.1 xlconcat_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xlslice:1.0 xlslice_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:util_vector_logic:2.0 util_vector_logic_0

parameters.name: CONFIG.CONST_VAL / CONFIG.CONST_WIDTH (xlconstant)
parameters.description: Constant value and its width in bits.

parameters.name: CONFIG.NUM_PORTS (xlconcat)
parameters.description: Number of inputs to concatenate; In0 becomes the least significant field.

parameters.name: CONFIG.IN<n>_WIDTH (xlconcat)
parameters.description: Width of input n, when the widths are not inferred from the connections.

parameters.name: CONFIG.DIN_WIDTH (xlslice)
parameters.description: Width of the input vector.

parameters.name: CONFIG.DIN_FROM / CONFIG.DIN_TO (xlslice)
parameters.description: Upper and lower bit index of the slice taken from the input.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_OPERATION (util_vector_logic)
parameters.description: and, or, xor or not.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_SIZE (util_vector_logic)
parameters.description: Vector width the operation is applied to; 1 for a single-bit invert.

tools.example:
# Invert an active-high reset for a core that wants active-low
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:util_vector_logic:2.0 rst_inv
set_property -dict [list CONFIG.C_OPERATION {not} CONFIG.C_SIZE {1}] [get_bd_cells rst_inv]
connect_bd_net [get_bd_pins processing_system7_0/FCLK_RESET0_N] [get_bd_pins rst_inv/Op1]

# Gather three interrupt sources into the PS interrupt port
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xlconcat:2.1 xlconcat_0
set_property CONFIG.NUM_PORTS {3} [get_bd_cells xlconcat_0]
connect_bd_net [get_bd_pins axi_gpio_1/ip2intc_irpt] [get_bd_pins xlconcat_0/In0]
connect_bd_net [get_bd_pins axi_dma_0/mm2s_introut]  [get_bd_pins xlconcat_0/In1]
connect_bd_net [get_bd_pins axi_dma_0/s2mm_introut]  [get_bd_pins xlconcat_0/In2]
connect_bd_net [get_bd_pins xlconcat_0/dout] [get_bd_pins processing_system7_0/IRQ_F2P]

# Tie an unused enable high
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xlconstant:1.1 const_1
set_property -dict [list CONFIG.CONST_WIDTH {1} CONFIG.CONST_VAL {1}] [get_bd_cells const_1]
tools.notes: The bit order of xlconcat matters for interrupt numbering: In0 is the least significant bit and therefore the lowest interrupt ID that software sees. util_vector_logic with C_OPERATION not and C_SIZE 1 is the idiomatic reset inverter in a block design; VLNV version suffixes vary by release.

tools.name: Arithmetic operators (floating_point, cordic, mult_gen, div_gen, cmpy)
tools.description: Generated arithmetic building blocks that map onto DSP slices and LUTs with a configurable latency/area trade-off. Floating-Point Operator covers add, subtract, multiply, divide, square root, compare and fixed/float conversion in single, double or custom precision; CORDIC computes trigonometric, hyperbolic, magnitude and square-root functions iteratively; Multiplier, Divider and Complex Multiplier generate the fixed-point equivalents. All of them present AXI4-Stream interfaces, so they drop straight into a streaming data path.
tools.usage:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:floating_point:7.1 floating_point_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:cordic:6.0 cordic_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:mult_gen:12.0 mult_gen_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:div_gen:5.1 div_gen_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:cmpy:6.0 cmpy_0

parameters.name: CONFIG.Operation_Type (floating_point)
parameters.description: Add_Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Square_root, Compare, Fixed_to_float, Float_to_fixed and similar.

parameters.name: CONFIG.A_Precision_Type (floating_point)
parameters.description: Single, Double or Custom; Custom exposes explicit exponent and fraction widths.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_Mult_Usage (floating_point)
parameters.description: No_Usage, Medium_Usage, Full_Usage or Max_Usage: how aggressively DSP slices are used instead of fabric.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Flow_Control
parameters.description: NonBlocking gives a fixed-latency pipeline with no back-pressure; Blocking honours TREADY at the cost of more logic.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Functional_Selection (cordic)
parameters.description: Rotate, Translate, Sin_and_Cos, Sinh_and_Cosh, Arc_Tan, Arc_Tanh or Square_Root.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Input_Width / CONFIG.Output_Width (cordic)
parameters.description: Operand widths, which together with Iterations set the achievable accuracy.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Multiplier_Construction (mult_gen)
parameters.description: Use_Mults to map onto DSP slices or Use_LUTs to build the multiplier in fabric.

parameters.name: CONFIG.PipeStages / CONFIG.C_Latency
parameters.description: Pipeline depth; deeper pipelines reach higher frequency at the cost of latency and registers.

tools.example:
# Single-precision multiplier as a standalone IP for hand-written RTL
create_ip -name floating_point -vendor xilinx.com -library ip -version 7.1 -module_name fp_mult
set_property -dict [list \
  CONFIG.Operation_Type {Multiply} \
  CONFIG.A_Precision_Type {Single} \
  CONFIG.C_Mult_Usage {Full_Usage} \
  CONFIG.Flow_Control {NonBlocking}] [get_ips fp_mult]
generate_target all [get_files fp_mult.xci]

# CORDIC sine/cosine generator inside a block design
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:cordic:6.0 cordic_0
set_property -dict [list CONFIG.Functional_Selection {Sin_and_Cos} \
  CONFIG.Input_Width {16} CONFIG.Output_Width {16}] [get_bd_cells cordic_0]
tools.notes: Latency is reported by the IP customisation GUI and depends on every parameter, so read it back rather than assuming; a change of precision or DSP usage silently shifts the pipeline depth and breaks any hand-balanced parallel path. NonBlocking flow control ignores TREADY entirely, which is efficient but means the downstream block must always be able to accept data. Product guides: Floating-Point Operator (PG060), CORDIC (PG105), Multiplier (PG108), Divider Generator (PG151), Complex Multiplier (PG104); VLNV version suffixes vary by release.

tools.name: DSP function generators (xfft, fir_compiler, dds_compiler)
tools.description: Larger signal-processing cores generated from a functional specification rather than assembled by hand. FFT implements forward and inverse transforms with a choice of architectures trading throughput against resources; FIR Compiler builds single-rate, interpolating, decimating and multi-channel filters from a coefficient vector and uses DSP slice time-sharing to exploit the ratio between clock rate and sample rate; DDS Compiler generates sine and cosine waveforms or acts as a numerically controlled oscillator. All three use AXI4-Stream for data and for run-time configuration.
tools.usage:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xfft:9.1 xfft_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:fir_compiler:7.2 fir_compiler_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:dds_compiler:6.0 dds_compiler_0

parameters.name: CONFIG.transform_length (xfft)
parameters.description: Number of points, a power of two from 8 up to 65536 depending on the architecture.

parameters.name: CONFIG.implementation_options (xfft)
parameters.description: pipelined_streaming_io for continuous throughput, radix_4_burst_io or radix_2_burst_io for smaller area, radix_2_lite_burst_io for the smallest.

parameters.name: CONFIG.scaling_options (xfft)
parameters.description: Scaled, unscaled or block floating point, which decides how internal growth is handled.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Coefficient_Vector (fir_compiler)
parameters.description: Comma-separated list of filter taps, normally produced by a design tool and pasted in.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Filter_Type (fir_compiler)
parameters.description: Single_Rate, Interpolation, Decimation, Hilbert or Interpolated.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Sample_Frequency / CONFIG.Clock_Frequency (fir_compiler)
parameters.description: Input sample rate and clock rate in MHz; their ratio determines how many taps can share one DSP slice.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Output_Selection (dds_compiler)
parameters.description: Sine, Cosine or Sine_and_Cosine.

parameters.name: CONFIG.Phase_Increment (dds_compiler)
parameters.description: Fixed, Programmable or Streaming, which decides whether the output frequency is compiled in or set at run time.

tools.example:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xfft:9.1 xfft_0
set_property -dict [list \
  CONFIG.transform_length {1024} \
  CONFIG.implementation_options {pipelined_streaming_io} \
  CONFIG.data_format {fixed_point} \
  CONFIG.scaling_options {block_floating_point}] [get_bd_cells xfft_0]

create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:fir_compiler:7.2 fir_compiler_0
set_property -dict [list \
  CONFIG.Filter_Type {Decimation} \
  CONFIG.Sample_Frequency {10.0} \
  CONFIG.Clock_Frequency {200.0} \
  CONFIG.Coefficient_Width {16}] [get_bd_cells fir_compiler_0]

connect_bd_intf_net [get_bd_intf_pins axi_dma_0/M_AXIS_MM2S] [get_bd_intf_pins xfft_0/S_AXIS_DATA]
connect_bd_intf_net [get_bd_intf_pins xfft_0/M_AXIS_DATA]    [get_bd_intf_pins axis_data_fifo_0/S_AXIS]
tools.notes: The FFT's S_AXIS_CONFIG channel must be written at least once before the first frame when a non-default scaling schedule or transform length is used, otherwise the core runs with its reset defaults. FIR Compiler reports the number of DSP slices it will use in the customisation GUI, and an over-sampled clock is what makes a long filter affordable. Product guides: Fast Fourier Transform (PG109), FIR Compiler (PG149), DDS Compiler (PG141); VLNV version suffixes vary by release.

tools.name: Memory and high-speed interface subsystems (ddr4, mig_7series, xdma, axi_ethernet, aurora_8b10b)
tools.description: Large subsystem IP that owns dedicated device resources: hard memory controllers and I/O banks for DDR, integrated PCIe blocks and gigabit transceivers for XDMA and Aurora, and the Ethernet MAC with its PHY interface. Each brings its own clocking, its own timing constraints and its own bank and transceiver location requirements, so they are configured early and the rest of the floorplan is arranged around them. All of them present AXI or AXI4-Stream to the rest of the block design.
tools.usage:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:ddr4:2.2 ddr4_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:mig_7series:4.2 mig_7series_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xdma:4.1 xdma_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:axi_ethernet:7.2 axi_ethernet_0
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:aurora_8b10b:11.2 aurora_8b10b_0

parameters.name: CONFIG.C0.DDR4_MemoryPart (ddr4)
parameters.description: Exact memory device part number, which sets the timing parameters of the controller.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C0.DDR4_DataWidth / CONFIG.C0.DDR4_AxiDataWidth (ddr4)
parameters.description: DRAM bus width and the width of the AXI user interface the fabric sees.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C0.DDR4_InputClockPeriod (ddr4)
parameters.description: Period of the reference clock in picoseconds; must match the board oscillator.

parameters.name: CONFIG.XML_INPUT_FILE (mig_7series)
parameters.description: Path to the MIG .prj file that holds the whole 7-series memory controller configuration, including pinout.

parameters.name: CONFIG.pl_link_cap_max_link_width / _speed (xdma)
parameters.description: PCIe lane count (X1 to X16) and generation speed, which must be supported by the selected transceivers.

parameters.name: CONFIG.axi_data_width (xdma)
parameters.description: Width of the AXI interface into the fabric, chosen to match the PCIe bandwidth.

parameters.name: CONFIG.PHY_TYPE (axi_ethernet)
parameters.description: Physical interface to the external PHY: MII, GMII, RGMII, SGMII or 1000BaseX.

parameters.name: CONFIG.C_LINE_RATE / CONFIG.C_AURORA_LANES (aurora_8b10b)
parameters.description: Serial line rate in Gb/s and the number of bonded transceiver lanes.

tools.example:
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:ddr4:2.2 ddr4_0
set_property -dict [list \
  CONFIG.C0.DDR4_InputClockPeriod {3332} \
  CONFIG.C0.DDR4_MemoryType {Components} \
  CONFIG.C0.DDR4_DataWidth {64} \
  CONFIG.C0.DDR4_AxiSelection {true} \
  CONFIG.C0.DDR4_AxiDataWidth {512}] [get_bd_cells ddr4_0]
make_bd_intf_pins_external [get_bd_intf_pins ddr4_0/C0_DDR4]

# PCIe DMA bridge, 8 lanes at Gen3
create_bd_cell -type ip -vlnv xilinx.com:ip:xdma:4.1 xdma_0
set_property -dict [list \
  CONFIG.pl_link_cap_max_link_width {X8} \
  CONFIG.pl_link_cap_max_link_speed {8.0_GT/s} \
  CONFIG.axi_data_width {256_bit}] [get_bd_cells xdma_0]

assign_bd_address
validate_bd_design
tools.notes: These cores deliver their own clocks (for example the DDR4 ui_clk and the XDMA axi_aclk) which usually become the clock for the whole subsystem around them, so plan the clocking from the memory or PCIe core outwards rather than from a clocking wizard. They also ship their own XDC, and their I/O bank and transceiver locations are fixed by the board, so the part and package must be chosen before configuring them. Product guides: UltraScale memory IP (PG150), 7 Series Memory Interface Solutions (UG586), DMA/Bridge Subsystem for PCI Express (PG195), AXI 1G/2.5G Ethernet Subsystem (PG138), Aurora 8B/10B (PG046). Exact CONFIG parameter names and VLNV version suffixes vary by device family and release, so confirm with report_property on the instance.
